targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: V3-EXQ-467e (2026-08-13): non_contributory -- did not score MECH-266. The 467d blockers are fixed and external_task occupancy is now reachable (1.0 at r=0.10 on every seed vs 0.0 everywhere in 467b/c/d), but AFFINITY_INPUT_CAP=2.0 over-corrects into bang-bang arbitration: a step function with occupancy ~1.0 at r=0.10 and exactly 0.0 at every r>=0.50, and n_switches == n_episodes (12) identical across a 20x rail sweep. Three measurement defects: the min-over-ratio-arms non-vacuity gate is anti-correlated with C1's own predicted effect (stronger hysteresis drives occupancy to 0 at high rails, failing the gate); the same min() conflates 'mode unreachable' with 'mode saturated', emitting a factually-false route_reason 'external_task_mode_not_occupied' when the mode is 100% occupied at r=0.10; and mean_dwell is mode-agnostic (all_run_lengths accumulates any mode change), so C1's monotonicity test compares external_task dwell at r=0.10 against internal_planning dwell at r>=0.50, where the rail no longer acts and the values are unmanipulated noise. Category standard, not substrate_ceiling.

recommended_substrate_queue_entry.severity_note: corrupting: the min()-based non-vacuity gate emits a route_reason that is factually false about the substrate state ('mode not occupied' when it is 100% occupied). recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint_update: SUPERSEDES the existing hint's direction. Next work is (a) determine whether a mixed regime exists at any cap (H1) or the discrete argmax register is structurally bang-bang (H2), and (b) restate the readiness gate per-arm/regime-conditioned rather than min-across-a-swept-range.

live_hypotheses: H1: cap mis-calibration -- some AFFINITY_INPUT_CAP (or per-signal caps) admits a mixed-occupancy regime; the arbiter can mix and the sweep has not found the operating point
H2: structural bang-bang -- SD-032a's discrete argmax mode register cannot produce graded occupancy at ANY cap; the cap relocates the step but never removes it
H3: instrumentation -- the non-vacuity gate and the mode-agnostic dwell statistic are ill-posed, so the verdicts are artefacts of the instrument rather than of the substrate

suggested_probes.sketch: sweep AFFINITY_INPUT_CAP across the full 3-seed curriculum; DV = per-arm fraction_in_external_task reported per-arm (never min). Null: no cap yields per-arm occupancy in (0.1, 0.9) on >= 2/3 seeds.

instrument the continuous salience aggregate MARGIN pre-argmax rather than the discrete mode label; characterise its distribution across caps. Null: the margin distribution is unimodal/graded, i.e. saturation is a cap artefact rather than structural.
re-score the BANKED 464e/467e data with a per-arm regime-conditioned occupancy gate and an occupancy-conditioned dwell statistic. No new run. Null: re-scoring changes no verdict.

fanout_recommendation.note: GOV-FANOUT-1. Run H3 FIRST -- it consumes only banked data and can invalidate the premises of H1/H2 before either burns compute. H2 is the leg that would otherwise never be asked: every prior experiment in this lineage read the discrete mode label, which is exactly the variable that cannot distinguish 'graded arbitration rendered discrete at the output' from 'arbitration discrete all the way down'.

learning_extracted: A non-vacuity gate built on min() across a SWEPT range is anti-correlated with the effect it gates when the sweep is designed to cross a transition; the matched statistic must be regime-conditioned, not minimised across the range.
A mode-agnostic dwell statistic is unsafe as a DV when occupancy is non-stationary across the sweep -- it silently changes which mode it summarizes mid-experiment.
min() over arms/ratios cannot distinguish 'mode unreachable' from 'mode saturated all-or-nothing'; both read 0.0, and the two imply opposite substrate fixes.

cluster_pattern.shape: Contact guard (absolute/negative-control precondition) PASSES 3/3 on both targets; the occupancy precondition that enables discrimination FAILS on both. Underneath, 19 of 21 arm/ratio cells sit at exactly 0.0 or exactly 1.0 fraction_in_external_task, with zero switches on every saturated-high cell and n_switches == n_episodes on every saturated-low cell.
cluster_pattern.structural_property: The SalienceCoordinator arbitrates BANG-BANG: after the salience_affinity_input_cap fix, external_task either wins totally or loses totally, with no mixed-occupancy regime anywhere in the swept range. Two structurally different tests (a 5-point dose-response sweep and a 2-arm contrast), with different DVs and different PASS shapes, running on substrate-identical code (the only diff between their substrate_commits is a phase3-queue snapshot of experiment_queue.json), return the same observation. The predecessors' failure was 'the mode is never occupied'; the successor's is 'the mode is only ever fully occupied or fully empty' -- a genuinely different signature produced by the fix for the first one.
cluster_pattern.readings_note: These force different planning decisions (calibrate the cap vs redesign the discrete mode register) and the banked data cannot separate them -- every observation to date is consistent with both. That is what makes this a discrimination rather than a single named build, and why routing is a GOV-FANOUT-1 portfolio.
